newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Hong Kong horse win ups Oakfields.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Hong Kong horse win ups Oakfields.

text.p: Oakfields Thoroughbreds and Leisure Industries Ltd said on Thursday its shares had surged on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange thanks to the victory of a South African horse in a premier Hong Kong race last weekend.

"The fact that London News won that race on Sunday in Hong Kong has shown that South African horses can compete with the rest of the world," said George Schauder, financial director of Oakfields, whose main business is breeding race horses.
Oakfields shares have this week surged to a high of 65 cents from a 38 cents close last Friday -- a leap of 71 percent. Stocks closed on Thursday at 60 cents after 42,500 shares changed hands.

The company signed a deal with the Guangzhou Jockey Club last December to supply up to 1,000 race horses a year to China for 15 years, which Schauder said could eventually be worth 15 million rand a year.
Oakfields has 40 percent of a joint venture with the Chinese club and will provide horses to be auctioned in China. The first 60 horses are now in quarantine ahead of shipment in next month.
"With the success of horse racing in Hong Kong, I think China is trying to follow suit. They were looking at companies in Britain, Ireland, Australia ... and they eventually chose us," Schauder said.
He said that because of a shortage of horses in South Africa, the company might have to source animals in Zimbabwe, Britain, Australia or New Zealand.
"Because of London News, people are now saying, 'perhaps that deal Oakfields has with China is quite a good deal'," Schauder said.
"We've got the horses, and obviously Oakfields will be able to get good prices for the horses, because the quality is good, that's what has sparked the share price movement," he said.
